name: badusb
description: BadUSB / Rubber Ducky payload encoder: base64-encodes a PowerShell script and wraps it in DuckyScript that opens Run→powershell, then decodes and executes via certutil
author: malwarekid (contrib) | secV

help.description: Generates a Rubber Ducky / HID attack payload from a PowerShell script. The .ps1 file is base64-encoded (via Python, no certutil needed on the attacker side), then the DuckyScript payload uses Win+R → powershell → certutil to decode and run it on the target. Output is a .txt file ready to flash to a USB Rubber Ducky or any compatible HID device.

examples: generate - encode .ps1 to DuckyScript payload file
preview  - same as generate but also prints the payload to stdout
encode   - return only the base64 of the .ps1 (no DuckyScript wrapper)

file_path.description: Path to the .ps1 PowerShell script to encode

output.description: Output file path for the DuckyScript payload (default: ~/.secv/badusb/<stem>_badusb.txt)

title.description: Payload metadata: title (added as REM comment)

description.description: Payload metadata: description (added as REM comment)

author.description: Payload metadata: author (added as REM comment)

version.description: Payload metadata: version (added as REM comment)

delay_after_ps.description: DELAY (ms) after PowerShell window opens - increase on slow targets

ducky_lang.description: Add 'DUCKY_LANG US' line (required for some firmware versions)

examples.description: Encode a PS1 reverse shell and save the DuckyScript payload
Preview the generated DuckyScript in terminal
Generate with full metadata headers and DUCKY_LANG
Get raw base64 of a PS1 for manual embedding

notes: Only .ps1 (PowerShell) files are supported as source
DuckyScript uses certutil -f -decode on the target - certutil is present on all Windows versions
Adjust delay_after_ps for slower hardware (try 1000-2000ms on cold machines)
Test payload timing in a VM before deploying on a real device
Compatible with USB Rubber Ducky, Hak5 devices, and any tool that accepts DuckyScript
payload.txt output is saved to ~/.secv/badusb/ by default
